requirements.requirement: HAProxy on node1 serves HTTP on port 80 and forwards / to a Node.js application listening only on loopback port 3000; the endpoint returns HTTP 200 with body infraset-nodejs.
requirements.summary: Before and after reboot, HAProxy was active and listening on *:80, while the backend listened only on 127.0.0.1:3000. Direct backend and HAProxy frontend requests both returned HTTP 200 with the exact required body. HAProxy configuration validation also succeeded.

requirements.requirement: Manage the Node.js application as infraset-nodejs.service.
requirements.summary: The named systemd service was loaded, enabled, active, and running the intended Node.js application. It remained enabled and recovered successfully after node restart.

overall_summary: Both public task outcomes are satisfied with direct functional evidence. The mandatory restart protocol is complete: node1 had a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged the restart, changed boot identity from ac73b359-243e-418e-b7bb-a7cff423e597 to 992ab083-fd34-440b-90b4-53d72869e0c0, and recovered its services, listeners, valid configuration, and HTTP behavior. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: Frontend behavior was tested from node1 using its managed IP rather than from an independent external client.
The fixed lifecycle listening-sockets observations were empty and therefore do not independently corroborate listener state; the executor's direct ss output supplies that evidence.
Three small final-response files remained under /tmp after evidence collection.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear task or mandatory restart-evidence purposes: package installation, creation of the restricted service account and application, systemd and HAProxy configuration, service enablement, and reboot. Package health remained clean and no failed services were observed. No causally unrelated troubleshooting mutation was identified. Minor retained residue consisted of three avoidable HTTP response files—/tmp/backend.after.body, /tmp/frontend.after.body, and /tmp/recovered.body—created while collecting final recovery evidence and not removed. Systemd private directories were expected consequences of the required service and reboot, not unnecessary mutations.
